intro: You're looking for equity release advisers near you because you want to understand whether releasing money from your home could work for your later life. Perhaps you've seen adverts or heard about lifetime mortgages and want someone local to explain the detail face to face. We can introduce you to an equity release adviser who covers your area, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for equity release advisers near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, local advice on whether equity release is right for them and what it would mean for their home and family.
needs: You own your home and are thinking about releasing some of its value to top up your retirement income.
You want to know how a lifetime mortgage differs from a home reversion plan and which might suit your circumstances.
You are concerned about the effect on your family's inheritance and want to discuss options openly with an adviser.
You need to understand the legal side, including why you will need your own solicitor before signing anything.
You would prefer to speak with an adviser who can visit you at home or meet locally rather than only over the phone.
context_heading: Understanding equity release advice and local availability
context: Equity release advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), and advisers must hold a specialist qualification. You can check any firm or adviser on the FCA register before you proceed. Most providers and advisers are members of the Equity Release Council, whose standards include protection from negative equity and the right to stay in your home for life.

When you search for advisers near you, you may find that some firms cover your area but are based elsewhere. It is worth asking whether they can meet you in person or whether advice is given remotely. You will also need your own solicitor to explain the legal documents before you sign, and many advisers encourage you to involve family members in the discussion.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for an equity release adviser near you so we can match you with someone who covers your area.
Give a brief idea of what you hope to achieve, such as supplementing your income or paying for home improvements.
Explain whether you have already looked into equity release or are just starting to explore it.
Say whether you would prefer a home visit, a local office meeting, or advice by phone or video.
Let us know if you would like family members to be involved in the discussions from the start.
Share any concerns you have, such as the impact on inheritance or the cost of advice, so the adviser can address them.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the equity release adviser
questions: Are you and your firm regulated by the FCA and on the FCA register?
Do you hold a specialist qualification in equity release advice?
Are you a member of the Equity Release Council, and what standards does that commit you to?
How do you compare a lifetime mortgage with a home reversion plan for my situation?
What alternatives to equity release should I consider before going ahead?
How will you involve my family in the discussion if I want them to be part of it?

faqs.q: How do I check that an equity release adviser is properly regulated?
faqs.a: You can check the firm or adviser on the FCA register. Equity release advice is regulated by the FCA, and advisers must hold a specialist qualification.

faqs.q: What is the Equity Release Council and why does membership matter?
faqs.a: The Equity Release Council is a trade body. Most providers and advisers are members, and its standards include protection from negative equity and the right to stay in your home for life.

faqs.q: Will I need a solicitor if I decide to go ahead with equity release?
faqs.a: Yes, you will need your own solicitor to explain the legal documents before you sign. Many advisers encourage you to involve family members in the discussion as well.

faqs.q: Can I speak to an adviser who is near me?
faqs.a: We can introduce you to an equity release adviser who covers your area. You can ask them whether they offer home visits or local meetings, or whether advice is given remotely.
